deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematical derivation on this page. It is a library request or loan slip (Bestellzettel), almost certainly for the Göttingen University Library. In ink, in Riemann's hand, it asks for three issues of the Journal de l'École polytechnique:
(a) Cahier 6, 'Paris an 7'. The Revolutionary year VII corresponds to 1798/99. A pencil note above, 'T. II', identifies it as Tome II.
(b) Cahier 15, 1809. Pencil adds 'T. 8.' (Tome VIII).
(c) Cahiers 35–36, dated '1855' in ink. A pencil correction or addition reads '1856', and the pencil note 'T. 20 21. 56' identifies Tomes XX–XXI.
It is signed 'B. Riemann', with a parenthetical word below that is probably an address or an identification. It reads approximately '(Westfal)' and remains uncertain.
The remaining marks are library or clerical annotations:
- a large pencil scrawl, perhaps initials or a shelf or processing mark, and a large pencil '4';
- the folio number '43';
- a red-crayon date, probably 'Nov. 22. 58' (possibly 'Jun.'), which is most plausibly the loan or return date, 22 November 1858.
Context (my inference, not on the page): Cahier 36 (Tome XXI, 1856) contains Briot & Bouquet's memoirs on functions defined by differential equations and on doubly periodic functions. That material relates directly to Riemann's 1857 work on Abelian and hypergeometric functions. The 1809 cahier contains Lagrange's and Poisson's memoirs on the variation of arbitrary constants in mechanics. I cannot confirm from the slip which articles Riemann wanted. The slip documents Riemann's reading or borrowing in late 1858 only.

transcription_corrections: The pencil 'T. II' stands above 'Cahier 6 ... Paris an 7': Cahier 6 = Tome II (an VII = 1798/99).
For Cah. 35–36 the ink date is '1855', with pencil '1856' (or '/1856') beside it; the pencil line below reads 'T. 20 21. 56'.
The red annotation is probably 'Nov. 22. 58.' (possibly 'Jun.'), likely a library date, 22.11.1858 (or 22.6.1858).
The parenthetical under the signature is uncertain; the machine reading '(Westfal)' is plausible, but the next-page reading 'Weißfisch' is not supported by the image.
The large pencil marks ('3[?]' scrawl and '4') are library/processing marks, not mathematics.
The next page is only mirror-image show-through of this slip; its 'E. Riemann' should read 'B. Riemann'.
